purpose: Which aggregation policies exist, which evaluator versions were meant to apply them, and which of those pairs a formal result may be attributed to. A policy file cannot say this: it does not know what code read it.
why_v2: v1 was pinned by hash and therefore could never gain a policy or an evaluator without breaking its own immutability rule. It also recorded no hash for the policy files themselves, so readiness had to be handed one by its caller and had no way to disagree. Each entry now carries the file and the bytes it must have.

statuses.active: the pair a run selects; formal results allowed
statuses.superseded: retired by a later version; kept byte-identical for the record
statuses.record_only: kept so anything recorded under it stays interpretable. No formal result was produced under it, and none may be

safe_sum_v1.note: superseded before any run reached it

safe_sum_v2.note: superseded before any run reached it

safe_sum_v3.note: four release paths found in review; see why_v4

safe_sum_v4.note: the explicit-total path never applied the axes the result claimed; see why_v5

note_on_growth: Adding a policy or an evaluator pair means a new registry version, because this file is pinned. That is deliberate: changing which pairs may publish is a change to what a result means, and should cost a version.
